newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Friday were steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by outlooks for light Saturday and Monday slaughter, livestock dealers said.
There also was talk that at least three large slaughtering plants would be closed on Monday for a floating holiday.
The weak packer demand offset potential support for cash hog prices from light marketings, they said.
"The hogs started slowing yesterday afternoon (Thursday) and have remained light this morning, but it doesn't matter because no one is fighting for them, " an Iowa hog buyer said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $1.00 per cwt lower at $58.00 to $58.50 in the country and $59.00 to $59.50 at plants, the livestock dealers said.
Illinois hogs sold steady at $59.00 to $59.50 in the country and $60.00 at plants, with some plants bidding $60.50 to $61.00 for premium hogs, they said.

Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower in light trading, with $57.50 paid in the country and $59.50 at plants. Ohio hogs were $1.00 lower at $57.00 in the country and $59.00 at plants, the dealers said.
